full_judgment: 2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule in short, is that, the opposite party Nos.I -2 as the preemptors filed the Preemption Miscellaneous Case No.10 of 2007 under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 alleging inter alia that Alfoo Bepari was original owner of 1.10 acres of land under C.S. Khatian No.324 C.S. Plot No.1528 Mouza No.46 present No.6 Dakhin Barha under District Dhaka Sub-registry officer Dohar under Touzi Dhaka Collectorate. Alfoo Bepari died leaving 2 sons namely I. Ukil Bepari and 2. Hazrat Ali Bepari as his heirs and their name were recorded in the SA and RS records. Abdus Sattar son of Hazrat All sold 5 decimal land to one Fazlur Rahman by a Suf Kabala deed No.368 dated 25.2.1997. Fazlur Rahman having been in possession of the said land as owner on 11.8.2004 sold 1.50 decimals land to the preemptors by a Suf —kabala deed and the preemptor became owner and possessions of the said land. Preemptee No.I on 29.5.2007 filled up the land by earth and the preemptors raised objection to this. He came to know that the pre-emptee No.2 sold the land to pre-emptee No.1. After obtaining certified copy of the deed pre-emptors came to know on 31.5.2007 that the pre-emptee No.1 purchased the land and he was the co-sharer of the case khatian land by purchase land from other co-sharer on 11.8.2004 and as such they are entitled to purchase the land 4 first and that the purchaser premptee was a stranger to case land for which he was not entitled to purchase the case land.
